title: Mizani's equivalent to scales' cut_short_scale/cut_long_scale()
description:
Hey!

I recently started using plotnine to replicate ggplot2's syntaxis in Python and it's been a great experience so far. I was just looking for the equivalents of scales's `cut_short_scale`/`cut_long_scale()` utils in the Minzani library but couldn't find any in the docs or the API. Haven't these been implemented yet or have their equivalents been named differently?

Thanks for the great work!

title: No way to ask `breaks_extended` for Talbot's loose labelings (`only.loose`)
description:
`breaks_extended` reproduces `labeling::extended` exactly on the default, but there
is no way to ask it for the covering labelings the reference implementation produces
with `only.loose=TRUE`.

The default is a faithful port. I ran 200 random `(dmin, dmax, m)` triples through
both and mizani matched R's `only.loose=FALSE` output element for element in all 200,
so this looks like a mode that did not come across rather than a porting error.

R's version:

```r
extended <- function(dmin, dmax, m, Q=c(1,5,2,2.5,4,3), only.loose=FALSE, w=c(0.25,0.2,0.5,0.05))
...
if(score > best$score && (!only.loose || (lmin <= dmin && lmax >= dmax)))
```

For data 1.6 to 5.1 at m=5, the two modes differ:

```r
extended(1.6, 5.1, 5, only.loose=TRUE)   # 1.5 2.5 3.5 4.5 5.5   brackets the data
extended(1.6, 5.1, 5, only.loose=FALSE)  # 2 3 4 5
```

No value of `only_inside` reaches the first one:

```python
from mizani.breaks import breaks_extended

for oi in (False, True, (True, False), (False, True)):
    print(oi, breaks_extended(n=5, only_inside=oi)((1.6, 5.1)))

# False          [2. 3. 4. 5.]
# True           [2. 3. 4. 5.]
# (True, False)  [2. 3. 4. 5.]
# (False, True)  [2. 3. 4. 5.]
```

`only_inside` is the opposite constraint rather than the same one, and it is a useful
mode the R package lacks, so between the two libraries there are three placements for
the extreme labels:

| placement | condition | R | mizani |
|---|---|---|---|
| inside | `lmin >= dmin and lmax <= dmax` | not available | `only_inside=True` |
| flexible (the default) | none | `only.loose=FALSE` | `only_inside=False` |
| loose | `lmin <= dmin and lmax >= dmax` | `only.loose=TRUE` | not available |

"Flexible" and "loose" are Talbot's own words for the middle and bottom rows, from
sections 3.1 and 2 of the paper.

Two shapes for adding the third, whichever suits the library better. A per-end
`only_loose: bool | tuple[bool, bool] = False` mirrors R and is the smaller change,
though it makes `only_inside=True, only_loose=True` on the same end representable and
unsatisfiable, so it would need a rule forbidding that. Alternatively a single
per-end parameter taking `"inside"`, `"flexible"` or `"loose"`, defaulting to
`"flexible"`, with `only_inside` kept as an alias mapping `True` to `"inside"` and
`False` to `"flexible"`. That leaves existing calls working unchanged and makes the
contradiction unrepresentable.

Happy to send a PR for either one.

title: `breaks_extended` never returns when a simplicity, coverage or density weight is 0
description:
```python
from mizani.breaks import breaks_extended

breaks_extended(n=5, w=(0.00, 0.20, 0.50, 0.05))((43.0, 96.0))  # simplicity
breaks_extended(n=5, w=(0.25, 0.00, 0.50, 0.05))((43.0, 96.0))  # coverage
breaks_extended(n=5, w=(0.25, 0.20, 0.00, 0.05))((43.0, 96.0))  # density
```

Each of these runs until I kill it, on mizani 0.14.6 and Python 3.12. I expected
either a labelling or a `ValueError`. What happens is no return, with
`RuntimeWarning: overflow encountered in scalar power` from `step = j * q * (10**z)`
along the way and the loop carrying on past it.

The three `while ... < float("inf")` loops in `__call__` exit only through their
pruning breaks, and each break's bound shrinks with exactly one weight: `w[0]` for
the `j` loop, `w[1]` for `z`, `w[2]` for `k`. At 0 that bound stops shrinking, so it
never drops below `best_score` and the loop has no exit. `w[3]` is unaffected because
`legibility` returns a constant, so zeroing it only prunes harder.

Negative values do the same for coverage and density. A negative simplicity weight
happened to return here, so 0 is the reliable trigger rather than non-positive
generally.

A guard in `__post_init__` would turn it into an error:

```python
if any(x <= 0 for x in self.w[:3]):
    raise ValueError(
        "the simplicity, coverage and density weights must be positive"
    )
```

Happy to send that as a PR.

title: numpy.timedelta DeprecationWarning on import from numpy>=2.5
description:
From numpy>=2.5.0 [release](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/releases/tag/v2.5.0) there is a DeprecationWarning on the generic `np.datetime64("NaT")` initialisation, which gets called when importing mizani._datetime.utils
```
import warnings

warnings.simplefilter("error", DeprecationWarning)

# DeprecationWarning: The 'generic' unit for NumPy timedelta is deprecated
import mizani._datetime.utils
```

yields:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "mizani/repro_script.py", line 6, in <module>
    import mizani._datetime.utils
  File "mizani/mizani/_datetime/utils.py", line 32, in <module>
    NaT_int = np.datetime64("NaT").astype(np.int64)
              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
DeprecationWarning: The 'generic' unit for NumPy timedelta is deprecated, and will raise an error in the future. This includes implicit conversion of bare integers (e.g. `+ 1`).Please use a specific unit instead.
```
I've put together a fix here: https://github.com/has2k1/mizani/pull/72

title: two tests from datetime/test_breaks.py fail with Python 3.14
description:
Fedora is preparing for shipping Python 3.14 with the next release. Testing the latest release of mizani with Python 3.14.0b3 revealed:

```python
=================================== FAILURES ===================================
____________________________ test_by_n_microseconds ____________________________

    def test_by_n_microseconds():
>       l1 = dt(("2025-01-01 01:10:30:000250", "2025-01-01 01:10:30:000600"))

tests/datetime/test_breaks.py:13: 
_ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ 
mizani/_datetime/utils.py:282: in dt
    return tuple(datetime.fromisoformat(x) for x in s)
_ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ 

.0 = <tuple_iterator object at 0x7fc7bd6731c0>

>   return tuple(datetime.fromisoformat(x) for x in s)
E   ValueError: Invalid isoformat string: '2025-01-01 01:10:30:000250'

mizani/_datetime/utils.py:282: ValueError
__________________________ test_by_width_microseconds __________________________

    def test_by_width_microseconds():
>       l1 = dt(("2025-01-01 01:10:30:000250", "2025-01-01 01:10:30:000600"))

tests/datetime/test_breaks.py:267: 
_ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ 
mizani/_datetime/utils.py:282: in dt
    return tuple(datetime.fromisoformat(x) for x in s)
_ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ 

.0 = <tuple_iterator object at 0x7fc7bcb6e170>

>   return tuple(datetime.fromisoformat(x) for x in s)
E   ValueError: Invalid isoformat string: '2025-01-01 01:10:30:000250'
```

Looking at the 3.14 changelog, the only change listed for `datetime` in Python 3.14 is the introduction of two new functions: `datetime.time.strptime()` and `datetime.date.strptime()`[^change]. That seems unrelated. But there might be some collateral change. I haven't taken a closer look yet.

title: Guidance on 'reversing' a transformation
Pseudolog transform
description:
Would be great to implement the pseudo log transform that also exists in the R `{scales}` package, because it's super useful for data that is best viewed on a logarithmic scale but which includes 0

The `{scales}` implementation is here

https://github.com/r-lib/scales/blob/04fc3331af14da0d5ca1919f37c6c35d6fc512bb/R/transform-numeric.R#L367C1-L375C2

Transform (in R) needs two params: `sigma` and `base`
```R
transform <- function(x) asinh(x / (2 * sigma)) / log(base)
inverse   <- function(x) 2 * sigma * sinh(x * log(base))
```

title: Comparison between tz-naive and tz-aware datetime objects due to `floor_hour` timezone erasure
description:
I haven't had time to find the exact conditions that trigger the condition described in the title, but from a little digging in my debugger, I found the following behavior in [`date_utils.py`](https://github.com/has2k1/mizani/blob/main/mizani/_core/date_utils.py):

```python
>>> floor_hour(datetime.datetime(2022, 12, 22, 8, 10, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc))
datetime.datetime(2022, 12, 22, 8, 0)
```
This effectively erases the timezone information. In my case, the return value is then compared to a timezone-aware datetime value from my dataset, which produces an error.

title: "ValueError: assignment destination is read-only" in .bounds.squish_infinite() with pandas CoW
description:

```
    l.draw(layout, coord)
  File "/opt/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.11.8/x64/lib/python3.11/site-packages/plotnine/layer.py", line 367, in draw

  File "/opt/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.11.8/x64/lib/python3.11/site-packages/plotnine/geoms/geom.py", line 289, in draw_layer
    self.draw_panel(pdata, panel_params, coord, ax, **params)

    self.draw_group(gdata, panel_params, coord, ax, **params)
  File "/opt/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.11.8/x64/lib/python3.11/site-packages/plotnine/geoms/geom_path.py", line 158, in draw_group
    data = coord.transform(data, panel_params, munch=True)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/opt/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.11.8/x64/lib/python3.11/site-packages/plotnine/coords/coord_cartesian.py", line 61, in transform
    return transform_position(data, squish_infinite_x, squish_infinite_y)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/opt/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.11.8/x64/lib/python3.11/site-packages/plotnine/positions/position.py", line 127, in transform_position
    data[xs] = data[xs].apply(trans_x)
               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/opt/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.11.8/x64/lib/python3.11/site-packages/pandas/core/frame.py", line 10034, in apply
    return op.apply().__finalize__(self, method="apply")
           ^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/opt/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.11.8/x64/lib/python3.11/site-packages/pandas/core/apply.py", line 837, in apply
    return self.apply_standard()
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/opt/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.11.8/x64/lib/python3.11/site-packages/pandas/core/apply.py", line 965, in apply_standard
    results, res_index = self.apply_series_generator()
                         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/opt/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.11.8/x64/lib/python3.11/site-packages/pandas/core/apply.py", line 981, in apply_series_generator
    results[i] = self.func(v, *self.args, **self.kwargs)
                 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/opt/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.11.8/x64/lib/python3.11/site-packages/plotnine/coords/coord_cartesian.py", line 56, in squish_infinite_x
    return squish_infinite(col, range=panel_params.x.range)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/opt/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.11.8/x64/lib/python3.11/site-packages/mizani/bounds.py", line 242, in squish_infinite
    _x[np.isneginf(_x)] = range[0]
    ~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
ValueError: assignment destination is read-only
```

My colleague @glatterf42 helpfully bisected and narrowed down the cause, which I summarize here:

- Pandas is moving towards "copy-on-write" (CoW 🐄), which will be default starting in version 3.0 (I am not sure when that will be released).
- They have [a documentation page with migration tips](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/stable/user_guide/copy_on_write.html#migrating-to-copy-on-write). 
- Although this is not yet the default, when one is using dask-expr (v1.0.1), a requirement for recent versions of dask[dataframe] (e.g. v2024.3.0), that package pre-emptively enables pandas copy-on-write. This seems to also be causing headaches for others, see dask/dask#10996.
- The result in mizani.bounds.squish_infinite() is that:
  - `x` is a pd.Series backed by read-only data.
  - `_x` is an np.ndarray reference to/view of that read-only data.
  - The above error occurs.

So I realize this issue is about a migration that mizani may have to make in the future, but at the moment it prevents simultaneous use of plotnine and dask[dataframe].

We will try to hack up a work-around (maybe forcibly disable copy-on-write just before a call to plotnine.ggplot.save()?) but wanted to give a heads-up.

title: Unable to load mizani.transforms on some platforms due to lack of system tzdata on some platforms
description:
On some platforms, the system does not provide `tzdata`, and this causes `import mizani.transforms` to result in an error.

For example, on recent versions of Pyodide, tzdata is not included. If you run the following in the [pyodide web console](https://pyodide.org/en/stable/console.html), it will result in an error.

```
>>> import micropip
>>> await micropip.install("mizani")
>>> import mizani
>>> mizani.__version__
'0.8.1'
>>> import mizani.transforms
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<frozen importlib._bootstrap>", line 995, in _find_and_load_unlocked
  File "<frozen importlib._bootstrap>", line 241, in _call_with_frames_removed
  File "<frozen importlib._bootstrap>", line 1053, in _gcd_import
  File "<frozen importlib._bootstrap>", line 1030, in _find_and_load
  File "<frozen importlib._bootstrap>", line 1007, in _find_and_load_unlocked
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tzdata'
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<console>", line 1, in <module>
  File "/lib/python3.10/site-packages/mizani/transforms.py", line 54, in <module>
    UTC = ZoneInfo('UTC')
  File "/lib/python3.10/zoneinfo/_zoneinfo.py", line 43, in __new__
    instance = cls._weak_cache.setdefault(key, cls._new_instance(key))
  File "/lib/python3.10/zoneinfo/_zoneinfo.py", line 70, in _new_instance
    file_obj = _common.load_tzdata(key)
  File "/lib/python3.10/zoneinfo/_common.py", line 24, in load_tzdata
    raise ZoneInfoNotFoundError(f"No time zone found with key {key}")
zoneinfo._common.ZoneInfoNotFoundError: 'No time zone found with key UTC'
```

The error comes from this line:
https://github.com/has2k1/mizani/blob/eb780650a0c9105e466ca03053bd9fe2c06cfd0a/mizani/transforms.py#L54

I believe that Windows also does not include tzdata by default, but I don't know for sure. [PEP 615](https://peps.python.org/pep-0615/#sources-for-time-zone-data) has something to say about this.


It is possible to make it work, by installing the `tzdata` module from PyPI. Running this in the pyodide web console will work:

```
>>> import micropip
>>> await micropip.install("mizani")
>>> await micropip.install("tzdata")
>>> import mizani
>>> mizani.__version__
'0.8.1'
>>> import mizani.transforms
```

I don't know what the best way is to specify a dependency on the tzdata module -- it doesn't seem like it should be a hard dependency, because it is only necessary if the system doesn't provide tzdata.

title: date_format doesn't support time formatting
description:
date_format returns zeros for `%H`, `%M` and `%S`

```
>>> from datetime import datetime
>>> import time
>>> from mizani import date_format

>>> fmt = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"

['2017-12-01 00:00:00']
```
